newsitem.title: BELGIUM: FULL TEXT OF GIB 1996/97 RESULTS.
newsitem.headline: FULL TEXT OF GIB 1996/97 RESULTS.

text.p: Following is the full text of the news release announcing GIB Group's 1996/1997 results. GIB GROUP REPORTS 8,9 % RISE IN GROUP SHARE OF OPERATING PROFIT

GIB GROUP has released preliminary details of consolidated earnings for the financial year ended on 31st January 1997. The final audited accounts and proposed dividend will be submitted to the meeting of the Board of Directors of 7th May 1997 and will be the subject of a later press release.
PRELIMINARY CONSOLIDATED RESULTS:
(KEY FIGURES TABLE OMITTED

GIB GROUP reported non-like-for-like consolidated turnover of BEF 216 557 million in 1996 (Fnac was sold in August 1996 and Handy Andy in October 1995), compared with BEF 227 780 million in 1995. Like-for-like turnover rose by 1.8 %.

Group share of operating profit rose by 8.9 % compared with 1995, due to the strong improvement in operating profit reported by GB and Scotty's and despite the serious deterioration in profitability at Sarma and Quick.
Current profit rose by 13.6 % as a result of the fall in net financial costs.

The extraordinary result of BEF 836 million mainly comprises capital gains on the sale of the Group's Homebase and Fnac interests, a provision in respect of discontinuing Sarma's activities and restructuring costs.
Group share of cash flow from operating activities was BEF 8 326 million against BEF 7 547 million in 1995, a rise of 10.3 %.
Group share of net profit was BEF 3 385 million, compared with a loss of BEF 4 385 million in 1995.
SUPERMARKETS AND HYPERMARKETS (67 % of total Group sales)
Sales within this sector (Super GB, Maxi GB, Unic, Nopri, Bigg's Continent, Rob and Globi) rose by 0.8 %.

GB increased its sales by 2.2 % compared with 1995, to BEF 110 197 million. Sales of food products rose by 3.3 %, while sales of non-food products declined by 0.5 % in a market which continued to suffer from weak consumer demand. GB maintained its market share for the second year running through various marketing measures.
GB has achieved a 22 % improvement in productivity in its stores since 1994. The chain invested over BEF 1.9 billion in 1996, mainly in renovating and enlarging its stores.
In 1997, GB will continue improving its product line-up, strengthening its customer service and enhancing management and productivity in its distribution centres.

Bigg's Continent increased sales by over 10 % at the Waterloo store. A new store was opened in Kuringen in June 1996. The partnership with Promodes has allowed the introduction of products from the Continent own-label range into the line-up.

Sales by the franchise chains Unic and Nopri totalled BEF 65 508 million. This is a fall of 3.5 %, due primarily to the closure of smaller stores no longer compatible with the new positioning of these chains.

Measures have been taken to achieve progressive enhancements in buying and logistical synergies among the GB, Unic and Nopri chains. The particularly competitively-priced range of "white label" products has been introduced into the Unic and Nopri line-ups. A common fresh produce distribution system has been set up to serve the three chains.
The commercial agreement with Promodes continues to reinforce the competitiveness of all the chains in this sector.

In Poland, Globi increased its sales by 29 % despite the arrival on the market of competing chains. International Finance Corporation, a subsidiary of the World Bank, took a 35 % shareholding in Globi in July 1996. D.I.Y. (18 % of total Group sales)
European D.I.Y. sales rose by 0.7 % despite inclement weather conditions for the gardening segment in the first half of the year.
D.I.Y. sales in Belgium remained stable at BEF 16 087 million. Brico has continued modernising its stores, reducing prices and improving its customer service.
A second Briko Depot store was opened at Antwerp in February 1996. The trial programme for this chain continued with the opening of a third store in Haine-St-Pierre a few days ago.

Auto 5, the car accessories and spare parts chain, continued its healthy progress and demonstrated the soundness of its service-focused positioning. Sales rose by 3.4 % to BEF 2 799 million. The chain is continuing its store modernisation programme.
In France, Obi maintained its turnover at BEF 8 023 million.
On the Iberian peninsula, Aki sales rose by 7.6 % to BEF 3 152 million. The chain opened 2 new stores in 1996, bringing the total to 16. The Group plans to open 4 more stores in 1997.

In Florida, Scotty's reported an increase of 3.1 % in Dollar sales. Combined with careful cost control, this has enabled the chain to double its operating profit to USD 12.5 million. Several stores were modernised and 21 neighbourhood hardware stores were opened in 1996.
RESTAURANTS (9 % of total Group sales)
Sales by the Group's restaurant chains rose by 8.8 %.

Quick increased its sales by 10 % and opened 54 restaurants in 1996, 45 of which are in France, 6 in Belgium, 2 in The Netherlands and 1 in Luxembourg. The crisis of consumer confidence over beef and the sluggish economic climate depressed profitability, which fell by 48 % to BEF 312 million. However, it is worth noting that Quick's cash flow fell by only 4 %.

Several measures have been taken to stimulate sales in the Quick chain and to launch it back onto its growth course. New chicken-based products have been introduced, marketing actions and promotional offers have been reinforced and a cost-reduction programme has been started.
The Quick chain will open 30 restaurants in 1997, including a fourth restaurant in The Netherlands.
Lunch Garden sales rose by 2.5 %. All the Group's cafeterias have operated under the Lunch Garden logo since 1996.
SPECIALITY RETAILING (6 % of total Group sales)
Sales by chains in this sector (Inno, Club, Pearle Vision and Disport) increased by 3.2 % to BEF 12 354 million.
Inno sales rose by 0.5 % to BEF 8 427 million.

Club, Pearle Vision and Disport achieved combined sales of BEF 3 927 million and continue to perform well. Club recorded a sales rise of 8 %, Pearle Vision sales were 8.6 % higher and Disport sales advanced by 11.3 %. These chains plan to open a total of 9 stores in 1997.
Sarma recorded an operating loss of some BEF 400 million in 1996. Sarma's business was discontinued in January 1997, when the Group agreed to let a majority of its stores to the Dutch chain Hema.
INVESTMENTS AND PRIORITIES FOR 1997
GIB GROUP plans to invest a total of almost BEF 7 billion during 1997 in support of its strategic objectives. The priorities for the year are:
1. To reinforce the competitiveness of GB, Unic, Nopri and Bigg's Continent

2. To redefine the local neighbourhood store concept 3. To develop the commercial agreement with Promodes 4. To continue the expansion of European D.I.Y. operations 5. To continue the recovery at Scotty's 6. To enhance the competitiveness of Quick and continue its growth.
Release ends
